data.title: Fusidic acid 2% cream
data.body:
_Topicals · II Antibacterials_

**Class:** Fusidane (steroid-like) antibiotic

## Mechanism of action
- Inhibits elongation factor G → stops bacterial protein synthesis
- Excellent penetration through intact skin and crusts; active against S. aureus (including many MRSA) and streptococci

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Impetigo, folliculitis, infected eczema, erythrasma, paronychia
- Combinations with steroid (fusidic acid + betamethasone/hydrocortisone) for infected eczema

## Dose & formulations
- Apply 3 times daily for up to 7–10 days (short courses limit resistance)

## Adverse effects
- Local irritation; rare contact dermatitis
- Rapid emergence of resistance with prolonged or widespread use

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe.

## Viva points
- EF-G inhibitor; steroid-like structure
- Resistance is a major problem — keep courses short
- Good penetration through crusts

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.41; Khopkar ch.18. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
